title: Poles of the Γ₀(5) scattering determinant lie in the band 1/16 ≤ Re s ≤ 7/16
statement: Let φ(s) = √π Γ(s − 1/2) ζ(2s − 1) / (Γ(s) ζ(2s)) be the SL₂(ℤ) scattering function and det Φ(s) = φ(s)² (26 − 5^{2s} − 5^{2−2s}) / (5^{2s} − 1)² the scattering determinant of Γ₀(5) (cusps ∞, 0; standard explicit Γ₀(p) matrix with p = 5). Claim: every pole of det Φ in the open strip 0 < Re s < 1/2 satisfies 1/16 ≤ Re s ≤ 7/16. Formal shape (Mathlib has no pole API): φ and det Φ are DifferentiableAt every s in the open strip with Re s ∉ [1/16, 7/16]. Under RH the band collapses to Re s = 1/4; the gap between the band and the line is RH itself, re-expressed for an object the programme already owns.

source.citation: Corollary of openai/math 003 (zero strip 1/8 ≤ Re ρ ≤ 7/8, via Brockian.QuasiRH003.riemannZeta_zero_strip) applied to the explicit Γ₀(p) scattering matrix (Hejhal; Huxley 1984; Iwaniec, Spectral Methods). Cross-check the constants against the Fricke-channel derivation in Structural_Theorems_Pass_3.

formal_targets.name: pole scan of det Φ on 0 < Re s < 1/2, |Im s| ≤ 50 (argument principle on small squares; every pole must sit at ρ/2 for an LMFDB zero ρ)

criteria: Targets A and B close with no sorry inside openai/math (Mode B), axioms ⊆ {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}
elementary factor: poles only on Re s = 0, zeros only on Re s ∈ {0, 1}; M_p(s)·M_p(1−s) = I (hand-checked 2026-10-07; re-derive against Pass 3)
numerical falsifier: no pole of det Φ off Re s = 1/4 for |Im s| ≤ 50 (any such pole falsifies the matrix, not the theorem)

notes: Decision this result changes: whether the Fricke-channel / scattering object becomes the first place in the programme where an external zero-free input is visible in the lab's own geometry — a theorem attached to the 'explanatory structure' organizing principle rather than a construction. Proof route for A: Γ(s−1/2), Γ(s) differentiable, Γ(s) ≠ 0 (Re s > 0, s ≠ 1/2); ζ(2s−1) differentiable (2s−1 ≠ 1); ζ(2s) differentiable (2s ≠ 1) and nonzero by riemannZeta_zero_strip at 2s (real part in (0,1) outside [1/8,7/8]); quotient rule. B adds 5^{2s} ≠ 1 from ‖5^{2s}‖ = 5^{2 Re s} > 1. Claims NOTHING about D₅, the golden ratio, the C₅ spectrum, or the C₂₀ reconstruction theorem; the band comes from 003's Eisenstein-field method, not pentagonal structure. Inherits 003's risk and adds none: a zero of ζ with Re ρ outside [1/8, 7/8] would falsify both. Blocked on math-openai-003-quasi-rh-import reaching PROVED (Mode B).
